corrections.reason: ISFDB (Ballantine hardcover H-135), 45worlds and Author Wars give March 1956 for the first printing; that month holds the confirmed Aeonos dive, so the book is left out. June is unsupported.

August is unsupported. Clarke’s own Times Higher Education article (29 Jun 2001) puts the accident and onset in the Feb-Mar 1962 window, six weeks in hospital, then England a few months later. Replaced by a verified 1962-02 cell (planning the dive).

notes: SECOND PASS. Web search quota ended partway, so some leads stayed open (listed below). Every cell here has an explicit month in a page I opened or in a search snippet; nothing is from memory. Where an upgrade keeps the first-pass text, only the month moved (or stayed) and the old placeholder month, when different, is in "corrections": 1956-09, 1965-09, 1972-08, 1973-04, 1974-04, 1974-09, 1975-09, 1979-01, 1980-04, 1980-08, 1983-11, 1984-07, 1986-04, 1988-06, 1989-05, 1989-11, 1989-12, 1990-10, 1992-06, 1992-11, 1993-06, 1993-07, 1994-11, 1996-03, 1997-03, 1999-08, 1999-12. summary.upgraded counts those 27 same-event cells; summary.new_confirmed counts the 34 other cells (some of them, e.g. 1956-05, 1962-02, 1963-08, 1984-09, 2000-04, replace a first-pass placeholder with a different, verified event; see corrections). With these the file has 81 + 27 + 34 = 142 confirmed months of 627 (22.6%). BOOK MONTHS: ISFDB cannot be fetched directly (Cloudflare 403), so its month-level publication records were read through search snippets only; ISFDB months sometimes come from Amazon or Locus and are single-source. Where UK and US editions differ I used the earliest edition ISFDB shows (usually Gollancz), except The Trigger, which sits at the US Bantam month (Dec 1999; ISFDB and Kirkus 1 Dec 1999) because the UK Voyager month (Nov 1999) holds the Nature story, and Richter 10 (Mar 1996: Bantam Spectra copyright note, Kirkus; ISFDB’s own Gollancz record shows both Feb and May 1996). Kirkus pages from the 1980s on show a separate Pub Date and review Issue date (3001: pub 12 Mar 1997, issue 1 Jan 1997; Hammer of God: pub 15 Jun 1993, issue 15 Apr 1993; McAleer: pub 1 Nov 1992, issue 1 Sep 1992), so 1st/15th pub dates there are usable as month-level dates. Kirkus’s dated entries for Imperial Earth (Jan 1975) and Fountains of Paradise (Jan 1978) have the wrong year (ISFDB: Gollancz Sep 1975, both hardcovers Jan 1979); only the Jan month agrees for Fountains. SHORT-STORY CELLS: months come from Wikipedia story infoboxes (pub_date) and from archive.org scans I opened: If Feb 1958 (contents list “Out From the Sun”), Galaxy Sep 1958 (full text lists “The Stroke of the Sun” by Clarke) and Galaxy Oct 1966 (contents list “A Recursion in Metastories”, the retitled “The Longest Science-Fiction Story Ever Told”). Venture to the Moon: Wikipedia infobox and ISFDB both give May 1956 (Evening Standard). Skipped for month collisions with confirmed cells: What Goes Up (F&SF Jan 1956), Saturn Rising (F&SF Mar 1961), Sunjammer/The Wind from the Sun (Boys’ Life Mar 1964), The Next Tenants (Satellite SF Feb 1957, same month as The Ultimate Melody), and Reach for Tomorrow (Ballantine Mar 1956 per ISFDB/45worlds, same month as the Aeonos dive). AWARDS: Nebulas are dated by the ceremony: 28 Apr 1973 (1972 awards, “A Meeting with Medusa”), 27 Apr 1974 (1973 awards, Rama), 26 Apr 1980 (1979 awards, Fountains), all from SFWA award-year pages as quoted in search snippets (SFWA pages redirect when fetched). Grand Master: SFWA says conferred 1985 with the ceremony in 1986; the sfadb page I opened lists the Claremont Hotel banquet on 26 Apr 1986 with Clarke as Grand Master. Hugos: Fancyclopedia (fetch blocked, read via snippet) gives the presentation as 1 Sep 1974 and 31 Aug 1980; for 1956 the lakdiva biography page I opened says Clarke took part in the Worldcon “in September of 1956” where “The Star” won, and Fancyclopedia puts the presentation on 3 or 4 Sep (Worldcon ran 31 Aug-3 Sep). LIFE EVENTS: 1962-02: Clarke’s own article “Painful memory of a silent stalker” (THES, 29 Jun 2001) says “In February 1962, I was planning a dive” before the head injury, overnight paralysis and six weeks in hospital; the exact day of onset is not given, so the cell is worded as the dive plan. 1984-09: McAleer’s biography excerpt (page opened) says Clarke videotaped a talk in Aug 1984 (opening with SDI, then a joint Mars mission) that was shown to the Senate Foreign Relations Committee on 17 Sep 1984; a library catalogue record dates that hearing (S. Hrg. 98-1064, “East-West cooperation in outer space”) 13 Sep 1984, so the month is solid but the “testified in person” claim is not. 1961-12: the Smithsonian accession record (7 Dec 1961, about 1000 silver rupees from the Great Basses wreck) is quoted on Kavan Ratnatunga’s lakdiva page, which names Clarke as donor; the same page captions a photo “seen in May 2003 reading” the Feb 1945 Wireless World. 1979-09: Clarke’s space-elevator address to the XXXth International Astronautical Congress, Munich, 20 Sep 1979, per the Wikipedia Space elevator reference list. 1996-11: Wikipedia Rama (video game) gives North American release Nov 1996 and says Clarke appears in it. 2000-04: Irish Times, 28 Apr 2000, “Author of ‘2001’ gets namesake” (Eutelsat dedicates its latest satellite to him). 2001-02, -09, -11: Clarke’s own “Egogram 2001” (signed 28 Dec 2001) says Roger Caras died on 19 Feb, he took part in a web discussion with Leonardo DiCaprio on 28 Sep, and appeared as a 3-D hologram at Comdex in Las Vegas on 13 Nov. 2001-03: Wikipedia 73rd Academy Awards lists Clarke as presenter (introduced by Tom Hanks), ceremony 25 Mar 2001. NEWS CELLS (Sunday Times of Sri Lanka): 7 Jun 1998 “Clarke honoured” (University of Illinois award; the page is dated), 1 Nov 1998 “A crerbral Marriage” (sic) by Richard Boyle, part one of a feature on Kubrick and Clarke making 2001 (the page is dated), 1 Sep 2002 “Sri Lanka is India without the hassle” (travel piece that visits his Colombo home; date taken from the 020901 URL, the page itself shows only a 2001 copyright footer) and 19 Mar 2006 “Tussle over time ticks on” (Clarke statement on the half-hour clock change; date from the 060319 URL, and the article’s April 14 change and “a decade” after 1996 fit 2006). The same URL convention matched the printed dates for the two 1998 pages. STILL UNVERIFIABLE (placeholders left as they were in the first pass, month unknown): The Reefs of Taprobane, Boy Beneath the Sea, Voice Across the Sea, The Challenge of the Spaceship (Kirkus 15 Jun 1959 only), Profiles of the Future (Kirkus 15 Jun 1962 vs ISFDB Gollancz 1962 and Harper 1963), Indian Ocean Treasure, Into Space, The Lost Worlds of 2001, The Best of Arthur C. Clarke 1937-1955 (ISFDB: Sphere 1976, no month) and 1956-1972 (1977), Report on Planet Three (ISFDB Gollancz Jun 1972 but a second record Jan 1973), The Light of Other Days, Childhood Ends (1996), Kalinga Prize (1961 vs UNESCO Courier 1962), Stuart Ballantine Medal, Marconi (a Nature notice reportedly dated Aug 1982 and the presentation by Prince Claus in The Hague could not be opened, so no month), resident guest status, post-polio diagnosis (1988, Johns Hopkins, year only), ISU chancellor, Marilyn Mayfield’s death. Washington Post archive items surfaced in search (16 Nov 1982 “The Galactic Dreamer Returns”, 9 Mar 1992 “Arthur C. Clarke’s Red Thumb”, 9 Jan 1999 “‘2001’ Writer Disputes Millennium’s Turn”) but the pages return 403 so they were not used. Gaps still empty: 1976, 1978, 1981, 1987, 1995 (no month-dated item found before the search quota ended). A 2025 BJHS article on Clarke and Sri Lanka (Cambridge Core) was fetched but its PDF text could not be decoded.
